subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters on the embedded attempt path, and what invalidation boundary should it use?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the permanent boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Land a narrow internal cache
options.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks and preserve fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared-runtime migration
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to avoid a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live repro before implementation
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main live Google/Gemini or heap proof showing the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks and preserve fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The cache lifecycle decision intersects the prepared-runtime migration foundation and tracker authored by this routing candidate.
